                             PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT

MEETING DATE:   November 17, 2022
PROJECT NUMBER: S-22-008
REQUEST(S):     A petition for a subdivision plat to consolidate twelve existing parcels into one parcel.
ADDRESS:        1015 West 3300 South, 1021 West 3300 South, 1035 West 3300 South, 1047 West 3300
                South, 1061 West 3300 South, 1111 West 3300 South, 3340 South 1000 West, 3360 South
                1000 West
PARCEL NUMBER:  15-26-377-001, 003, 004, 005, 006, 008, 009, 010, 011, 013, 015, 019
PROPERTY OWNER: Salt Lake County
APPLICANT:      Tracy Aviary

SYNOPSIS:
The Tracy Aviary is petitioning the
Planning Commission for a
subdivision plat application to
consolidate    twelve      existing
parcels located at 1111-1015
West 3300 South and 3340-3360
South 1000 West into one parcel.

The Tracy Aviary is proposing to
expand their existing Nature
Center Pilot Project area at James
Madison Park from 0.45 acres to
an expansion of 11.99 acres. The
nature center would include
numerous gardens and amenities
such as an amphitheater, a nature
center, a café, and a rope course.

The subject property is currently
comprised of James Madison
Park, the Tracy Aviary Nature Center Pilot Project Area, vacant land, portions of un-programmed Jordan River
corridor and four single family homes.

The Planning Commission is the Land Use Authority on all subdivision plat applications.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends approval to the Planning Commission to approve a subdivision plat to consolidate twelve
existing parcels into one parcel. Staff’s recommendation is based upon its analysis and findings included below.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:

17.11.030. Land use authority designations.
Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

   A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of: subdivision and
      subdivision plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision Plat; Conditional Use permit
      Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this Title; design review for projects
      on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the issuance of a Building
      or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.



                                                       10
GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS:


Community Values Goal 4. Enhance community pride and identity.
     Analysis: The proposed project will improve the streetscape along both 3300 South and 1000 West. It
     will also add a valuable amenity unique to this community.

Parks, Recreation, & Open Space Goal 1. Increase the number and acreage of parks, open space, and recreation
amenities to serve current and future residents.

       Analysis: The proposed project will increase the open space available to residents, and will add recreation
       amenities that are unique to this site.

Parks, Recreation, & Open Space Goal 3. Continue to provide equitable access to city programs and amenities
for all residents.

       Analysis: The proposed project will add amenities and open space to one of only two parks located west
       of I-15 in South Salt Lake.

Jordan River Commission Best Practices for Riverfront Communities, Introduction. Open space in the vicinity
of the river can act as a buffer between natural areas and development. These actively managed areas have
potential to improve the overall function and quality of the Jordan River, including enhancing native vegetation
and improving stormwater management. These improvements will not only enhance recreation and scenic value
of the area, but also provide valuable ecosystem services.

       Analysis: The proposed project will primarily consist of open space and will both act as a natural buffer
       and provide ecosystem services.

Jordan River Commission – Best Practices for Riverfront Communities, Recreation Goal 3. Integrate active
recreation that maintains river function and wildlife. Integrating recreational areas into natural systems can help
improve urban runoff, infiltrate rainwater, and improve flood management while also providing contact with nature
and beautiful landscapes.

       Analysis: The proposed project will integrate native species, which will contribute to a sense of place and
       help reduce contaminants into the Jordan River.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the
relevant code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to approve,
with conditions, the final subdivision plat amendment and proposes the following findings of fact and
conclusions of law and conditions of approval:

Findings of Fact:

    1.   The subject properties, located at 1015 West 3300 South, 1021 West 3300 South, 1035 West 3300
         South, 1047 West 3300 South, 1061 West 3300 South, 1111 West 3300 South, 3340 South 1000 West,
         3360 South 1000 West, consist of twelve separate lots.
    2.   All twelve lots are located in the Tracy Aviary’s Jordan River Nature Center (JRNC) zone.
    3.   The proposed subdivision will consolidate twelve existing lots located at 1015 West 3300 South, 1021
         West 3300 South, 1035 West 3300 South, 1047 West 3300 South, 1061 West 3300 South, 1111 West
         3300 South, 3340 South 1000 West, 3360 South 1000 West.
    4.   The proposed subdivision will create one lot that will be 11.99 acres in size.
    5.   The property owner is applying for the subdivision to construct a nature center.
    6.   The proposed development will be located in the JRNC land use district.
    7.   The proposed building falls into the Nature Center land use category.
    8.   The Nature Center use is a permitted land use in the JRNC zone.
                                                      14
   9.    The subject property currently consists of James Madison Park, the Tracy Aviary Nature Center Pilot
         Project Area, vacant land, portions of un-programmed Jordan River corridor and four single family
         homes.
   10.   The proposed lot will be served by existing and new vehicular and pedestrian access points on 3300
         South and 1000 West.
   11.   Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Section “17.10.140
         Subdivision Development Lot Standards” and found that this subdivision is compliant with this section,
         as outlined above.
   12.   Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Section “17.10.150
         Subdivision and Condominium Plat Layout Requirements” and found that this subdivision is compliant
         with this section, as outlined above.
   13.   Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Sections 17.10.160,
         17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190, 17.10.200, and 17.10.210, and found that this subdivision is compliant
         with those sections, as outlined above.

Conclusions of Law:

   1.    The subdivision, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General
         Plan.
   2.    The subdivision, as specifically conditioned below is compatible in use, scale, and design with the
         allowed uses in the JRNC zone.
   3.    The subdivision as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare
         of: Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the
         vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the proposed
         use or development.
   4.    The subdivision, as specifically conditioned below does not impose disproportionate burdens on the
         citizens of the city.

Conditions of Approval:

   1.    The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior to
         recording;
   2.    Prior to plat recordation and any additional development of the subsequent lot, the applicant must
         provide city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to dedication;
         obtain signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;
   3.    The applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant and
         post required warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure improvements;
   4.    The applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements of
         the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code;
   5.    The applicant shall dedicate an easement to the City of South Salt for purposes of storm water
         management practices and ensure the plat includes language of the dedication of such easement, in a
         form as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;
   6.    The proposed building shall be constructed according to South Salt Lake commercial design standards;
   7.    The plans shall provide a fencing plan that is constructed according to South Salt Lake commercial
         design standards;
   8.    All items of the staff report.

PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:


   Option 1: Approval
   Move to approve the application by Tim Brown, on behalf of Tracy Aviary for a preliminary subdivision plat
   amendment for the twelve-lot subdivision consolidation of the subject properties located at 1015 West 3300
   South, 1021 West 3300 South, 1035 West 3300 South, 1047 West 3300 South, 1061 West 3300 South, 1111
   West 3300 South, 3340 South 1000 West, 3360 South 1000 West, with the conditions enumerated in the staff
   report and on the record.
                                                       15
   Option 2: Denial
   Move to deny the application by Tim Brown, on behalf of Tracy Aviary for a preliminary subdivision plat
   amendment for the twelve-lot subdivision consolidation of the subject properties located at 1015 West 3300
   South, 1021 West 3300 South, 1035 West 3300 South, 1047 West 3300 South, 1061 West 3300 South, 1111
   West 3300 South, 3340 South 1000 West, 3360 South 1000 West, for the reasons stated on the record.

   Option 3: Continuance
   Move to table the decision on the application by Tim Brown, on behalf of Tracy Aviary for a preliminary
   subdivision plat amendment for the twelve-lot subdivision consolidation of the subject properties located at
   1015 West 3300 South, 1021 West 3300 South, 1035 West 3300 South, 1047 West 3300 South, 1061 West
   3300 South, 1111 West 3300 South, 3340 South 1000 West, 3360 South 1000 West to a date certain to allow
   the Applicant and Staff time to respond to specific inquiries or concerns raised by the Planning Commission,
   or to allow the Planning Commission more time to consider the proposal.

                               PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE:                  November 17, 2022
PROJECT NUMBER:                S-22-007
REQUEST:                       A petition to the Planning Commission for a preliminary subdivision plat
                               amendment to consolidate two existing lots into one lot.
ADDRESS:                       3167 South 300 West and 3175 South 300 West
PARCEL NUMBER:                 15-25-403-007-0000 and 15-25-403-008-0000
PROPERTY OWNER:                O-Zone Biotech, LLC
APPLICANT:                     Jared Peterson

 SYNOPSIS:
 On behalf of O-Zone Biotech, LLC, Jared Peterson is petitioning the Planning Commission for preliminary
 approval of a subdivision plat amendment to the Liberty Acres subdivision plat to consolidate two existing
 parcels into one parcel located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175 South 300 West.

 The south parcel has one commercial building where Idaho Molecular is located. The parcel to the north is
 the park lot for Idaho Molecular.

 The Planning Commission is the Land Use Authority on all subdivision plat applications and amendments.

    TOD                                                                                       300 West
                   Office            Office      S ½ of Lot 17: 0.24         acres
                                                        acres


STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission vote to approve a preliminary subdivision plat amendment
to consolidate two existing lots into one lot located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175 South 300 West.
Staff’s recommendation is based upon its analysis and findings included below.

 PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:
 17.11.030. Land use authority designations.
 Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

    A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of: subdivision
    and subdivision plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision Plat; Conditional Use
    permit Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this Title; design review for
    projects on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the issuance of a
    Building or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.


GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS:
 Land Use & Neighborhood Strategy 8. Appropriately seek the redevelopment of legal non-conforming
 uses, properties, and structures to be more conforming over the long term.

     Analysis: This lot consolidation will create off-street on-site parking to the existing building. Currently
     the existing building has two on-site parking shall, which does not comply with the parking requirement.

                                                      7
STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission approve the preliminary subdivision plat amendment to
consolidate two existing lots into one lot located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175 South 300 West, with
the following conditions:

Findings of Fact:

   1. The subject property is located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175 South 300 West.

   2. The lots are located within the TOD land use district.

   3. The proposed subdivision will consolidate two lots into one lot.

   4. The new lot will be 0.48 acres in size.

   5. These lots are compliant with the standards in the TOD zone, which does not contain specific
      minimum area standards for a commercial lot.

   6. The subject property currently has a professional office land use.

   7. Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Section “17.10.140
      Subdivision Development Lot Standards” and found that this subdivision is compliant with this
      section.

   8. Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Section “17.10.150
      Subdivision and Condominium Plat Layout Requirements” and found that this subdivision is
      compliant with this section as conditioned.

   9. Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Sections 17.10.160,
      17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190, 17.10.200, and 17.10.300, and found that this subdivision is
      compliant with those sections as conditioned, as outlined above.

Conclusions of Law:

   1. Based on the findings above, the Planning Commission has good cause to approve the subdivision
      plat amendment.

Conditions of Approval:

   1. The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior
      to recording the plat;

   2. Prior to plat recordation and any additional development of the subsequent lot, the applicant must
      provide city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to
      dedication; obtain signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;

   3. Complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant and post required
      warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure improvements;

   4. The plat shall include language dedicating an easement to the City of South Salt for purposes of
      storm water management practices, in a form as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;

   5. All site improvements shall be installed consistent with the requirements of the South Salt Lake
      City Municipal Code;

                                                     8
   6. All items of the staff report.


PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:
   Option 1: Approval
   Move to approve the application by O-Zone Biotech, LLC, for a preliminary subdivision plat amendment
   to consolidate two existing lots into one lot located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175 South 300 West
   with the conditions enumerated in the staff report and on the record.

   Option 2: Denial
   Move to deny the a the application by O-Zone Biotech, LLC, for a preliminary subdivision plat
   amendment to consolidate two existing lots into one lot located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175
   South 300 West with the conditions enumerated in the staff report and on the record.

   Option 3: Continuance
   Move to table the decision on the application by O-Zone Biotech, LLC, for a preliminary subdivision plat
   amendment to consolidate two existing lots into one lot located at 3167 South 300 West and 3175
   South 300 West, to a date certain, for the reasons stated on the record and to provide the applicant
   and staff more time to provide more information as requested by the Planning Commission in order to
   make the decision.

                             PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE:                November 17, 2022
REQUEST:                     A resolution of the City of South Salt Lake City Council adopting the annual
                             Moderate Income Housing Plan Report to the State of Utah.
APPLICANTS:                  South Salt Lake City

 SYNOPSIS:
 Staff is proposing an amendment to the South Salt Lake General Plan 2040 to comply with state
 requirements for moderate income housing. The Utah State Legislature passed House Bill 462 (HB 462)
 in March of 2022, requiring that municipalities take additional steps to ensure that each municipality is
 planning for and reducing barriers to moderate income housing. Moderate income is defined as those
 persons/families with household incomes less than eighty percent (80%) the area median income (AMI).
 HB 462 requires that municipalities include certain strategies in the Moderate Income Housing elements
 of their general plans and provides a list of twenty-four “menu” items to select them from. HB 462 also
 requires that cities develop actionable implementation plans for each of those strategies that include a
 timeline for each strategy within the next five years.

 The Planning Commission is the recommending body for amendments to the general plan and the City
 Council is the land use authority for amendments to the general plan.


PROJECT INFORMATION:
South Salt Lake is required to select and adopt at least five strategies. Staff recommends that we adopt the
five strategies listed below. The current South Salt Lake General Plan 2040 only requires a small amount of
tweaking to meet HB462 requirements.

Staff has completed a thorough review of all the moderate income housing strategies (the 24 menu items)
within HB462 and found that the South Salt Lake General Plan 2040 already contains similar strategies
that can be found throughout the entire plan.

Due to the similar strategies, being throughout the entire plan Staff has found the appendix the most
applicable area to include the new strategies and implementation plan. The appendix currently houses the
2020 Moderate Incoming Housing Plan.


PROPOSED STRATEGIES AND IMPLEMENTATION ELEMENTS:

(E) Strategy 1: Create, or allow for, and reduce regulations related to, internal or detached accessory
dwelling units in residential zones
Implementation Action:

   •   Identify areas of the city with appropriate infrastructure, amenities, and services to support
       detached accessory dwelling units; and
   •   Work with the South Salt Lake City Council and appropriate South Salt Lake City Staff to create
       and implement an ordinance for detached accessory dwelling units in residential zones by 2024.

                                                     1
(F) Strategy 2: Zone or rezone for higher density or moderate income residential development in
commercial or mixed-use zones near major transit investment corridors, commercial centers, or
employment centers

Implementation Action:

   •   Coordinate with Wasatch Front Regional Council on developing and adopting station area plans
       for the Meadowbrook, Millcreek, and Central Pointe UTA TRAX Stations, as well as the 500 East,
       300 East, and South Salt Lake City S-Line stops. At least four of these station area plans will be
       completed by December 31, 2025.
   •   Revisit annually and revise as appropriate South Salt Lake’s transit-oriented development (TOD)
       land use plans, policies, and zoning provisions to measure effectiveness and consistency with the
       goals of the general plan and with the moderate income housing strategies outlined here. Primary
       methods should include:
           o Revisiting TOD boundaries;
           o Reviewing current residential density maximums; and
           o Promoting transit supportive design and appropriate density to leverage transit oriented
               development along TRAX, streetcar, and key bus hubs; and
   •   Revisit annually and revise as appropriate South Salt Lake’s commercial zone policies and zoning
       provisions to measure effectiveness and consistency with the goals of the general plan and with
       the moderate income housing strategies outlined here. Primary methods should include:
           o Evaluating potential locations for higher residential densities in commercial zones, primarily
               guided by the future land use map in the General Plan;
           o Carefully excluding areas that have the highest potential as thriving commercial hubs; and
           o Evaluating potential incentive-based policies to attract moderate to low-income housing
               developments.



(H) Strategy 3: Amend land use regulations to eliminate or reduce parking requirements of residential
development where a resident is less likely to rely on the resident’s own vehicle, such as residential
development near major transit investment corridors or senior living facilities
Implementation Action:

   •   Revisit annually and revise as appropriate South Salt Lake’s transit-oriented development (TOD)
       land use plans, policies, and zoning provisions to measure effectiveness and consistency with the
       goals of the general plan and with the moderate income housing strategies outlined here;
   •   Consider permitting tandem parking in appropriate areas;
   •   Revisit annually and revise as appropriate South Salt Lake’s current parking reduction
       requirements; and
   •   Revisit annually and revise as appropriate South Salt Lake’s shared parking schedule.



(Q) Strategy 4: Create a housing and transit reinvestment zone pursuant to Title 63N, Chapter 3, Part 6,
Housing and Transit Reinvestment Zone

Implementation Action:

   •   Create a housing and transit reinvestment zone surrounding the Central Pointe TRAX Station by
       2024.

                                                     2
(V) Strategy 5: Develop and adopt a station area plan in accordance with Section 10-9a-403.1

Implementation Action:

   •   Coordinate with Wasatch Front Regional Council and other appropriate agencies on developing
       and adopting station area plans for the Meadowbrook, Millcreek, and Central Pointe UTA TRAX
       Stations, as well as the 500 East, 300 East, and South Salt Lake City S-Line stops. At least four of
       these station area plans will be completed by December 31, 2025.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends the Planning Commission forward a recommendation of approval to the City Council for
the resolution to adopt the annual Moderate Income Housing Plan Report.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:

17.11.010. Establishment and Duties of Planning Commission.

   K. Responsibilities.

       A. The Planning Commission makes recommendations to the City Council for:
             a. The general plan and amendments to the general plan;
             b. The Land Use Map, and amendments to the Land Use Map;
             c. Amendments to land use ordinances;
             d. Proposed Application processes and the delegation of power under the land use
             ordinance.

PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:
Option 1: Approval

   Move to forward a recommendation of approval to the City Council for a resolution to adopt the annual
   Moderate Income Housing Plan Report.
Option 2: Denial

   Move to forward a recommendation to the City Council to deny a resolution to adopt the annual
   Moderate Income Housing Plan Report.
Option 3: Continuance

   Move to table the recommendation to the City Council for a resolution to adopt the annual Moderate
   Income Housing Plan Report.

                                                                 HOUSING VISION STATEMENT

                                 “ South Salt Lake is a community where residents are housed in safe, cared-
                                   for, and healthy neighborhoods that are connected to parks, local shopping,
                                   services, and regional transportation. Residents living in South Salt Lake have a
                                   choice of housing types that align with their household type, age, lifestyle, and
                                   budget to support our diverse families and residents. Housing opportunities in
                                              South Salt Lake are affordable to a variety of households.”

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE FUTURE:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Develop and maintain an affordable and attainable supply of housing for all
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              income levels by incentivizing diverse housing development/rehabilitation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Encourage the development of housing that ranges in size and scale to
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              accommodate the needs of all residents.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Encourage residents to stay in place through the provision of City-
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              supported initiatives and increased code enforcement to make needed
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              repairs, upgrades, and promote property maintenance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Ensure that all residents have access to retail, services, and neighborhood
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              amenities that are easily and safely accessible by foot, bike, or transit.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Support the creation of advisory neighborhood councils to improve

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Promote neighborhood pride and a unique sense of place to create
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              lifelong residents and to attract new residents.

                                                                                                                        PSYCHOGRAPHICS
                                                                                                                        Psychographics are critical in understanding a population's attitudes and interests rather than being limited by “objective”
                                                                                                                        demographics. While demographics can tell us about a household’s size and average income, psychographics can help to
                                                                                                                        paint a picture of why that family may purchase a particular item, or have preferences related to technology. These sorts of
                                                                                                                        insights enable people to find similar-interest households, linking those with similar interests and attitudes, even if they’re from
                                                                                                                        a different community. Below is a summation of the top psychographic segments based upon the percentage of households

     Salt Lake based upon a capture rate closely aligned with historical building permits ,Table
     B-6. The analysis shows the County is projected to gain over 5,850 total new households
     annually over the next five years. The majority of household growth in the County is
     anticipated to be driven by the age groups of 35 - 54-year old’s, and the 65 and over
     community.

     Based on qualified earners and owner propensity throughout the County, this regional
     growth has potential to create demand for 3,679 new households. Based on the qualified
     earners and turnover rate of existing owner-occupied households within the County, there
     are 12,566 estimated owners that will purchase upon moving. Turnover of existing rental
     households based upon qualified incomes and propensity to purchase upon moving will
     generate additional demand for 12,46 transactions. The total potential projected demand
     for new home purchases throughout the County is 16,246.

     Across all income categories, our projections show that South Salt Lake has the potential
     to capture 325 new buyers annually based on a conservative capture rate. Based upon
     affordability of new buyers there is demand for 55 percent of the total new homes valued
     between $200,000 and $450,000. In addition, income levels also show a moderate need
     for housing above $450,000.

                      South Salt Lake has significantly expanded its bicycle and trail network in recent years. The need
                      for trails and bike lanes is highly location specific, and by necessity should consider regional routes,              MAP 3:
                      continuous routes and key connections. There are limited opportunities to put continuous routes
                      through the city, and these opportunities need to be identified and protected. The City is planning
                      to update its transportation master plan and write and Active Transportation Plan, in order to create a               TRAILS AND BIKE LANES
                      more robust pedestrian and bike network. The city is also preparing a Sidewalk Master Plan to identify
                      major gaps in the pedestrian network and appropriate solutions. Of particular importance is working                                              TRAILS & BIKE LANES
                      with UTA on strategies to get transit riders easily to and from stations. Connections to Salt Lake City
                      trails, bike routes and sidewalks is another priority. Residents have also suggested building a bike
                      share kiosk in some parts of the city to allow for short-term rentals and to connect to the Salt Lake City
                      “green bike” system.                                                                                                                                                                          2100 S

                      On a larger scale, the City is working with Salt Lake County on a East-West Trails Master Plan that                                                        INDUSTRIAL
                      identifies new major priority projects. The Parley’s Trail route is one priority, and the plan suggests
                      connecting from the Wasatch Mountains to the Oquirrh Mountains.

                      South Salt Lake has three major multi-use trail routes and a small number of unmarked primitive trails
                      in natural open space areas. One new route, the Meadowbrook is emerging along 3900 South. Parley’s
                      Trail and the Jordan River Parkway are managed primarily by Salt Lake County, but do or may include
                      small city-owned sections.

                                                                                                                               ventures. Many amenities can also be provided by developers within their private projects. However,
